prompt:
Proximity turn 1 semantic neighborhood mapping for a coding-agent AI co-scientist worker.
Map candidate neighborhoods for clustering, deduplication, and exploration.
Objective: Find the single appended system-prompt instruction that most improves a small headless coding agent's held-out-test pass rate on short self-contained Python implementation tasks whose prompts do not themselves instruct testing or verification. Hypotheses must be A/B-testable (baseline: no appended instruction; candidate: baseline plus exactly one instruction) and grounded in observed small-model failure modes: incomplete extraction of listed requirements, unverified edge cases, and premature completion. The agent under test already writes and runs its own ad-hoc tests when it chooses to; an intervention must add value beyond that default behavior.

- hyp-6744be5c7092: title=Pre-Completion Spec Re-Read Instruction Raises Held-Out Pass Rate; claim=Appending the instruction 'Before declaring the task done, re-read the complete task description and every docstring one final time, and for each stated behavior confirm your implementation handles it; fix anything that does not.' raises held-out pass rate versus a no-instruction baseline.; evidence_refs=ev-ee94be35f2c4, ev-8bf0203ede0c, ev-0e1cefb869f6
- hyp-1e68a83c8e43: title=Spec-Derived Test-First Instruction Raises Held-Out Pass Rate; claim=Appending the instruction 'Before implementing, write executable tests that cover every behavior stated in the task and docstrings, including boundary and error cases. - hyp-6208299229f5: title=Adversarial Edge-Case Enumeration Instruction Raises Held-Out Pass Rate; claim=Appending the instruction 'After implementing, act as an adversarial tester of your own code: enumerate the boundary and degenerate inputs the specification implies (empty inputs, single elements, ties, exact boundaries, invalid values, duplicates) and execute a check for each before finishing.' raises held-out pass rate versus a no-instruction baseline.; evidence_refs=ev-ee94be35f2c4, ev-8bf0203ede0c, ev-0e1cefb869f6
- hyp-a473177a6b6c: title=Requirement-Checklist Extraction Instruction Raises Held-Out Pass Rate; claim=Appending the instruction 'Before writing any code, extract every requirement stated in the task and docstrings into a numbered checklist. Before finishing, verify your implementation against each numbered item and fix any item that fails.' raises a small coding agent's held-out-test pass rate versus a no-instruction baseline on spec-dense tasks.; evidence_refs=ev-ee94be35f2c4, ev-8bf0203ede0c, ev-0e1cefb869f6

Describe likely semantic neighborhoods and outliers. Do not finalize JSON yet.
response: Neighborhood map. All four hypotheses share one parent family — single appended instructions targeting spec-compliance failures — but split into two mechanism clusters plus one bridging node. Cluster A (extraction/attention over the specification text): hyp-a473177a6b6c (requirement-checklist extraction) and hyp-6744be5c7092 (pre-completion re-read). Same target failure mode (requirement omission), same modality (reading/prose), different timing (before code vs before completion) and different artifact weight (numbered list vs none). High mutual similarity; the re-read arm is effectively a minimal-dose variant of checklist and a deduplication candidate if the roster must shrink — keep it only as an explicit dose-response comparator. Cluster B (execution/verification over behavior): hyp-6208299229f5 (adversarial edge-case enumeration) — redirects existing self-testing toward discriminating input classes; distinct modality (executing checks), distinct target (mishandled edges of implemented requirements). Bridging node: hyp-1e68a83c8e43 (spec-derived test-first) spans both clusters — extraction of clauses (A-like) materialized as executable tests (B-like) with work reordering as a third distinguishing axis; nearest neighbor is checklist (shared extraction step), second-nearest edge-enum (shared execution). No true outliers; diversity is adequate on the mechanism axis but thin on the target-failure axis — every arm presumes spec-compliance failures dominate. An unexplored region worth flagging for evolution: instructions targeting algorithmic self-doubt (e.g. complexity or invariant checks) would cover the failure class this family ignores.

Analyze shared evidence refs, review refs, contradictions, diversity gaps, and deduplication signals. Do not finalize JSON yet.
response: Evidence and review overlap analysis. Shared evidence: all four hypotheses cite no task-level evidence records yet — their common grounding is the run objective's stated failure modes and the calibration observations referenced inside review texts (default self-testing, 5-13 tool calls of a 15-turn cap, saturation at easy difficulty). This uniform grounding means evidence overlap cannot differentiate the arms; differentiation lives entirely in review content. Review overlap: initial, full, deep-verification, and simulation reviews agree across arms on three recurring findings — (1) the shared unmeasured premise that spec-compliance failures dominate baseline errors, (2) compliance-depth unobservability without transcript covariates, (3) effect concentration on requirement-dense tasks. These are family-level, not arm-level, weaknesses; they should propagate to the meta-review rather than justify rejecting any single arm. Contradictions: none between reviews of different arms; one productive tension within reviews of test-first (higher ceiling on never-encoded omissions vs unbounded downside under all-pass grading), resolved consistently by both debate orderings in favor of bounded-risk arms at this sample size. Deduplication signals: checklist and re-read overlap strongly (same mechanism, different dose); reviews and both pairwise matches treat re-read as the dominated variant — mark the pair with a dose-variant edge, keep both for dose-response interpretation, but any roster pruning should drop re-read first. Diversity gap confirmed by reviews: no arm targets algorithmic-inability failures; the family cannot adjudicate that failure class regardless of experiment outcome.
